headline: Computational mining expands known viral diversity and host range predictions
label: Computational Viral Genome Discovery
summary: Public sequence archives and genomic language model embeddings now enable large-scale discovery of uncharacterized viruses and their hosts.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational analysis of viral sequence and structure data to expand or sharpen what is known about viral diversity, function and host association. Mining of public short-read archives with a Snakemake pipeline and a two-stage ML classifier yields 32+ putative novel tobamoviruses. VHAMSTeR predicts viral hosts across five kingdoms using fine-tuned genomic language model embeddings combined with genome and protein features. KSS scores viral k-mers by combining an information-theoretic discriminative measure, a GA-optimized MIYATA_EVO substitution matrix and a UniProt-based component. Structural-alphabet searches and structure similarity networks reveal diverse GT-A glycosyltransferases across double-stranded DNA viruses and a candidate sulfation-related jumbo-phage enzyme. The H5Nx study adds a caution: genotype assignments based on genetic similarity are incongruent with global phylogenies.
